title: content.replace on WordPress words the theme prints at render time names the gate that kept the rendered-words road shut (all:true → retry with all:"page"; outside the main region; a page with no record of its own; an older plugin), on known and untraced themes alike, instead of the generic 'cannot replace them through a door yet'
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/replace-wordpress-rendered-words.test.mjs packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/replace-wordpress.test.mjs
S2: Read the exit code, the `# pass`, `# fail`, `# skipped` and `# cancelled` lines and the tests named below.
expect: S1 exits 0 with 0 failures, 0 skipped, 0 cancelled.

'all:true on words the theme prints on this page names its gate and all:"page", nothing written' passes, and 'the same sidebar words with all:"page" change through the rendered-words road, one apply' passes.
'all:true on an older plugin says the plugin is older, never sends the call round with all:"page"' passes.

'words the theme prints outside the main region say so, never the generic sentence', 'on a known theme, words the theme prints in the header name the outside gate too' and 'on a known theme, a page with no record of its own names that gate' pass.
'a reason with a road of its own keeps its next: the theme file on a page with no record' passes.
evidence: Issue #1677 (24/10/2026): on a JA Restaurant WordPress demo, content.replace {all:true} on the /blog/ sidebar banner words answered NOT_EDITABLE with the generic 'cannot replace them through a door yet'; the same call with all:"page" changed them. The banner is printed by the theme's PHP into the sidebar of /blog/ only.
fence: Mechanism only: the WordPress replace engine over the package's fake component. Not covered: a live site with the real plugin, and whether the model follows the new next.
